questions.q: The 2026 Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences was awarded 'for microeconomic foundations of macroeconomic stabilisation' to
o: Daron Acemoglu, Simon Johnson and James Robinson
Joel Mokyr, Philippe Aghion and Peter Howitt
Robert E. Hall and Michael Woodford
questions.e: Robert E. Hall (Stanford) and Michael Woodford (Columbia) won in 2026. The other options are earlier laureates (2024, 2025 and 2004; static GK). Stabilisation means using fiscal and monetary policy to damp swings in growth and unemployment, an idea that came from Keynes during the Great Depression.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: Keynes argued that savings are not automatically converted into investment.
Statement-II: Keynesian demand management proved effective in curing the stagflation of the 1970s.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect. For Keynes investment depends on expected profit, and investment generates the income that produces equal saving. The oil-shock stagflation of the 1970s, with high inflation and high unemployment together, made Keynesian intervention look like part of the problem, prompting the search for micro foundations honoured by the 2026 Nobel.

questions.q:
With reference to the recent rise in edible-oil prices, consider the following statements:
1. The FAO Food Price Index averaged 136 in September 2026, the highest since November 2022.
2. FAME biodiesel is produced by transesterification of vegetable oils with methanol.
3. India imports about one-third of its edible-oil requirement.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. India imports about 60% of its edible oil, and imports are projected at a record 17.2 million tonnes as domestic output falls. The 'triple trigger' is conflict, El Nino droughts and biofuel mandates: roughly a quarter of soybean oil and 28% of palm oil now go to biodiesel, and Indonesia moved to B50 in July 2026.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. El Nino-linked drought reduces oil-palm yields after a lag of about 8-12 months.
2. Soybean oil is the largest item in India's projected edible-oil imports.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 1 is correct; palms abort flowers under drought, so output falls months later, as in Indonesia (58.5 to 56.6 million tonnes). Palm oil leads India's projected imports (8.2 mt) followed by soy (5 mt) and sunflower (3.5 mt). Record Russian and Ukrainian sunflower crops are stuck because of Black Sea strikes and the closure of the Sea of Azov.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding municipal property tax in India:
1. Collections are about 0.15-0.2% of GDP, below the average for low-income countries.
2. Studies in cities such as Bengaluru, Pune and Ghaziabad found weaker tax revisions when municipal elections were delayed.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Both are correct. Low-income countries average about 0.3% of GDP and middle-income countries 0.6%. Chennai did better with permanent assessors. The chain is enumeration, valuation and billing; GIS, satellites and drones help, but the magazine stresses physical verification, skilled staff, regular elections and realistic valuation.

questions.q: In the context of the global employment crisis, the term 'premature deindustrialisation' refers to
o: countries shifting from manufacturing to services at lower levels of income than today's rich countries did
the closure of factories before they repay their capital costs
the shift of manufacturing from developed to developing countries
a decline in manufacturing output caused only by recession
questions.e: It describes manufacturing's share of jobs peaking earlier and at lower income levels, partly due to automation, which weakens the manufacturing-led route to absorbing labour. The World Bank expects 1.2 billion Global South youth to reach working age in a decade; Shankar cites about 400 million jobs, while the Recitals cites 420 million over 10-15 years.

questions.q:
With reference to India's Model Bilateral Investment Treaty, consider the following statements:
1. The 2015 Model followed the White Industries Australia v. India award of 2011.
2. The 2015 Model requires investors to pursue local remedies for five years before international arbitration.
3. India's investment treaties with the UAE and Israel retain the five-year local-remedies period.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The UAE and Israel treaties use a three-year period, part of a more flexible approach. The revision announced in Budget 2025-26 weighs MFN scope, investor obligations and State counterclaims, mediation in line with UNCITRAL's ISDS reform, and a shift from protection to investment facilitation.

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
Item : Associated with
1. Maffezini v. Spain : Use of an MFN clause to import more favourable dispute-settlement procedures
2. UNCITRAL Working Group III : Drafting the WTO Investment Facilitation for Development Agreement
3. White Industries Australia v. India : Award that prompted India's 2015 Model BIT
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: Pairs 1 and 3 are correct. UNCITRAL Working Group III deals with reform of investor-State dispute settlement, including mediation; the IFD Agreement is a WTO plurilateral (static GK). Plama v. Bulgaria took the opposite view to Maffezini on MFN and procedure, which is why India's revision seeks a clearly limited MFN clause.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding household finances in India:
1. Net household financial savings fell between 2023-24 and 2024-25.
2. Household debt rose from 42% of GDP in June 2023 to 45.5% in September 2025.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 2 is correct. Net household financial savings rose from 5.2% of GDP in 2023-24 to about 6% in 2024-25. The concern is fast growth in unsecured credit (personal loans, cards, digital lending), a shift from savings-led to credit-led consumption, and borrowing for essentials by informal workers with uneven incomes.

questions.q:
With reference to agriculture in India, consider the following statements:
1. The Ashok Dalwai Committee estimated that doubling farmers' income needs annual agricultural growth of about 10.4%.
2. India's agricultural exports in 2025-26 exceeded its agricultural imports.
3. The PM Dhan-Dhaanya Krishi Yojana focuses on low-performing agricultural districts.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: All three are correct. Agri exports were about $53 billion against imports of about $40 billion, mainly edible oils and pulses. Agricultural GDP has grown about 4% a year since 2014-15, well short of the Dalwai target. India has surplus rice and wheat but shortfalls in pulses and oilseeds, and about 7 mt of rice goes to ethanol.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding agri-photovoltaics:
Statement-I: Agrivoltaic installations mount solar panels at a height of about 10-11 feet with spacing so that crops can be grown beneath them.
Statement-II: Shading from the panels can reduce heat stress and water loss for crops.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Both statements are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I: the panels are raised to allow farming and machinery underneath, while lower heat stress is an added benefit. An ICRIER pilot in Rajasthan raised a farmer's income 8-10 times. The magazine suggests adapting PM-KUSUM with PM-Surya Ghar-style subsidies and predictable feed-in tariffs.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding converting petrol and diesel vehicles to electric:
1. Section 52 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 prohibits any alteration of a registered vehicle.
2. Rule 115D of the Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989 applies only to CNG conversion kits.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Neither is correct. Section 52 regulates alterations and permits approved conversions, and Rule 115D provides for hybrid and electric retrofitment. Retrofitting keeps the chassis and replaces the powertrain, offering a cheaper EV transition and a circular economy; the magazine proposes certified retrofit centres modelled on PM Surya Ghar's empanelled-vendor network.

questions.q:
With reference to the Eastern Maritime Corridor, consider the following statements:
1. It links Mumbai with Vladivostok.
2. Russia's Trans-Arctic Transport Corridor is meant to connect with India through the EMC in the west and the INSTC in the east.
3. Scheduled direct liner services already run weekly on the route.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: None is correct. The EMC links Chennai with Vladivostok; Russia's Trans-Arctic Transport Corridor connects with India through the INSTC in the west and the EMC in the east. There are no scheduled direct services yet; cargo is transhipped via Ningbo or Shanghai. The route is about 10,470 km (24 days) against 16,070 km via Suez, with freight over 50% cheaper.

questions.q:
With reference to Green Energy Corridor Phase-III approved by the Cabinet, consider the following statements:
1. It mainly strengthens inter-State transmission corridors.
2. It aims to evacuate up to 135 GW of renewable energy by 2032-33.
3. It includes 50 GWh of battery energy storage.
4. Greenfield projects are to be awarded through tariff-based competitive bidding.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Statements 2, 3 and 4 are correct. Phases I and II focused on inter-State corridors such as the Raigarh-Pugalur HVDC link; Phase III targets intra-State networks in RE-rich States, implemented by STUs. The total outlay is Rs 1,86,405 crore, including Rs 50,000 crore for storage, with central financial assistance of Rs 54,082 crore.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: Solar power in India is increasingly curtailed even when there is demand for it.
Statement-II: Solar plants can be built in 12-18 months, while transmission lines often take 12-24 months or more.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Both are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I. About 21 GW runs on Temporary General Network Access, 12 GW of it with peak-hour limits. The sources give different periods: Shankar cites about 6,900 GWh curtailed in FY 2025-26, the Recitals 8,133 GWh of solar in April-June 2026; they should not be mixed. Batteries at congestion nodes help.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding 3D concrete printing in construction:
1. India's first 3D-printed house was built by IIT Madras and the start-up Tvasta in 2021.
2. In 3D concrete printing, foundations, roofs and plumbing are printed by the same robotic printer as the walls.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 1 is correct. The printer extrudes concrete layer by layer from a BIM model converted into G-code, mainly for walls; foundations, reinforcement, roofs, plumbing, wiring and fittings remain conventional. Andhra Pradesh's PMAY-G pilot will build 177 rural houses, each in about 45-60 days, but codes and durability data are still lacking.

questions.q:
With reference to the National River Linking Project, consider the following statements:
1. It envisages 30 links between river basins.
2. Inter-basin transfers can act as an 'ecological highway' for invasive alien species and aquatic pathogens.
3. Climate change makes the fixed classification of basins as 'surplus' or 'deficit' more reliable over time.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Climate change undermines fixed surplus and deficit labels. The project covers 37 basins and about 174 BCM of transfer. The Lower Ganga already has 13-15 invasive species and the Mahanadi 69 threatened species; remedies include basin-level EIA covering invasives and biosecurity monitoring.

questions.q:
With reference to cloud computing in India, consider the following statements:
1. MeghRaj, the GI Cloud initiative, was launched by NITI Aayog.
2. Storing data within India by itself ensures full data sovereignty.
3. MeitY's Cloud Selection Framework of March 2026 guides choices according to data sensitivity.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 3 is correct. MeghRaj was launched by MeitY in 2014, and MeghRaj 2.0 covered 2,330 departments by September 2026. The magazine stresses that domestic storage alone is not full control, given foreign technology dependence. Data-centre capacity of 1.57 GW in August 2026 is projected to reach 8 GW by 2030.

questions.q:
With reference to the Regional Connectivity Scheme UDAN, which completed ten years in 2026, consider the following statements:
1. Operational airports in India rose from 74 in 2014 to 166.
2. Its network includes heliports and water aerodromes.
3. Under the Modified UDAN scheme, viability gap funding can be given to a route for up to ten years.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct; the 95 aerodromes include 17 heliports and 2 water aerodromes. VGF of Rs 10,043 crore is spread over ten years, but each route gets support for up to five years, tapering from year three, with three years' exclusivity. UDAN was launched in 2016 under the National Civil Aviation Policy.

questions.q: Under the institutional framework of the PM GatiShakti National Master Plan, the Empowered Group of Secretaries (EGoS) is chaired by the
o: Chief Executive Officer of NITI Aayog
Principal Secretary to the Prime Minister
questions.e: The plan has three tiers: the EGoS under the Cabinet Secretary, the Network Planning Group, and a Technical Support Unit, with DPIIT's Logistics Division as secretariat. Launched in 2021, it covers 58 ministries and all 36 States and UTs on a GIS platform; by August 2026 the NPG had evaluated 396 projects worth about Rs 18.66 lakh crore.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Integrated Transport and Logistics Authority approved by the Cabinet:
1. It replaces the Network Planning Group under PM GatiShakti.
2. It is a special purpose vehicle for research, planning, appraisal and monitoring across transport and logistics.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 2 is correct. ITLA complements PM GatiShakti and the National Logistics Policy; GatiShakti keeps its three tiers, the Empowered Group of Secretaries, the NPG and the Technical Support Unit. ITLA is modelled on bodies in Korea, Japan, the US, China and Australia and will build a data repository for Vision 2047.

questions.q: The 'Trade and Development Report 2026: The Geoeconomics of Development' is published by
o: the United Nations Conference on Trade and Development
questions.e: UNCTAD publishes the TDR. It puts 2026 global growth at 2.6% with Asia supplying about 59%; India is projected at 7.3%. China-US trade has fallen over 20% since 2024, and AI products now drive goods trade. Strategic sectors rose from 16% to 44% of greenfield FDI in 2020-25, mostly to developed economies.

questions.q:
With reference to UNCTAD's Trade and Development Report 2026, consider the following statements:
1. Asia accounts for about 59% of global growth.
2. Between 2022 and 2025, India introduced more industrial-policy measures than the US and China.
3. Developing economies lead announced greenfield FDI projects only in critical minerals among strategic sectors.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. India adopted 1,416 measures in 2008-21 (behind China's 4,201 and the US's 4,025), and its 707 measures in 2022-25 were overtaken by the US, China, Australia and Brazil. Developed economies take about 70% of strategic-sector projects; developing ones lead only in critical minerals (60%).

questions.q:
With reference to the strategic sale of IDBI Bank, consider the following statements:
1. The buyer, Fairfax Financial Holdings, is a Canadian company.
2. The entire 60.72% stake being sold is held by the Government of India.
3. After the sale, neither the Government nor LIC will retain any stake in the bank.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 1 is correct. The 60.72% comprises 30.48% from the Government and 30.24% from LIC, sold for about Rs 52,878 crore at Rs 81 a share; the Government keeps 15% and LIC 19%. Fairfax must exit or merge CSB Bank within two years. The deal takes FY27 disinvestment to Rs 82,301 crore against an Rs 80,000 crore target.

questions.q: The Department of Investment and Public Asset Management (DIPAM), which runs strategic disinvestment such as the IDBI Bank sale, functions under the
questions.e: DIPAM is a department of the Ministry of Finance. Strategic disinvestment transfers management control, unlike a minority stake sale. In the IDBI case bidders needed an RBI fit-and-proper check and MHA security clearance, and thin trading meant valuation by market-multiple and asset-valuation methods; unions object to the loss of public control.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding Infrastructure Investment Trusts (InvITs) under the SEBI InvIT Regulations, 2014:
1. A public InvIT must invest at least 80% of its assets in completed, revenue-generating projects.
2. A public InvIT's investment in under-construction projects is capped at 10%.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Both are correct. The remaining 20% can go to under-construction projects (within 10%), infrastructure debt, equity of firms earning at least 80% from infrastructure, or government securities and money market instruments; private InvITs can mix freely. Listed InvITs grew from 2 in FY17 to 28 in FY26, with AUM of Rs 7.3 lakh crore.

questions.q: India's first social bond dedicated to water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH), listed on the NSE in October 2026, was issued by
o: Small Industries Development Bank of India
questions.e: NABKISAN Finance, a NABARD subsidiary, raised Rs 180 crore for five years at a coupon of 8.10%, maturing in September 2031, with Water.org as adviser and AAA ratings from CRISIL and CARE. A social bond raises money for projects with social outcomes, here household water and sanitation.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding PNG Drive 3.0 and the incentive scheme for domestic piped natural gas:
1. Gas distributors get an additional quantity of cheaper APM gas for each incremental billed domestic connection.
2. States have been urged to raise VAT on natural gas to 18%.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 1 is correct: 200 SCM of APM gas per incremental billed connection. States were urged to cut VAT on gas to 5%. The PNGRB drive (1 October 2026 to 31 March 2027) targets 50 lakh new connections and 40 lakh conversions to active users, with uniform right-of-way charges under the 2026 Pipelines Order.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: Corporate Average Fuel Efficiency (CAFE) norms prescribe a separate fuel-consumption limit that every car model must meet.
Statement-II: CAFE norms are notified under the Energy Conservation Act, 2001.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct. CAFE sets a fleet-average limit on fuel consumption or CO2 for a manufacturer's sales, not a limit per model. First introduced in 2017, Phase III notified by the Ministry of Power applies to passenger vehicles from 1 April 2027 to 31 March 2032, covering cars made or imported for sale.

questions.q:
With reference to the Annual Survey of Industries 2024-25, consider the following statements:
1. It is conducted by the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation.
2. Tamil Nadu has the largest number of factories.
3. Maharashtra accounts for the highest gross value added.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: All three are correct. Factories rose from 2.60 to 2.67 lakh, GVA by 9.59% and employment from 1.96 to 2.10 crore. Tamil Nadu (41,221 factories) is followed by Gujarat and Maharashtra; in GVA Maharashtra leads Gujarat, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka and UP. The survey covers factories under the Factories Act, 1948, among others.

questions.q: The Rebate of State and Central Taxes and Levies (RoSCTL), extended in October 2026, applies to exports of apparel and 'made-ups'. 'Made-ups' refers to
o: non-garment textile articles such as bed linen, curtains and towels
handloom fabric sold by the metre
questions.e: Made-ups are non-garment textile articles. The Ministry of Textiles extended RoSCTL from 1 October to 31 December 2026; running since 2019, it zero-rates exports by refunding embedded State and Central levies. In 2025-26 over 15,400 exporters in 444+ districts, mostly MSMEs, used it.

questions.q:
With reference to India's accession to the Southern Indian Ocean Fisheries Agreement (SIOFA), consider the following statements:
1. India is moving from the status of a cooperating non-contracting party to that of a Contracting Party.
2. The SIOFA secretariat is located in Victoria, Seychelles.
3. India has been a Contracting Party of the Indian Ocean Tuna Commission since 1996.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. SIOFA is headquartered at Le Port, Reunion; Victoria hosts the IOTC (static GK). Accession lets Indian vessels fish non-migratory high-seas stocks such as squid, toothfish and alfonsino, and gives seats on the scientific and compliance committees; Indian boats mostly fish within 60-80 nm today.

questions.q:
Which of the following are registries under AgriStack in the Digital Agriculture Mission?
1. Farmers' Registry
2. Crop Sown Registry
3. Soil Health Registry
4. Geo-referenced Village Maps
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: AgriStack has three registries: the Farmers' Registry, Geo-referenced Village Maps and the Crop Sown Registry. Soil Health Cards are a separate scheme. India issued 11 crore Farmer IDs, Aadhaar-like and linked to land records, five months before the March 2027 target.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the soybean varieties NRC 268 and NRC 270:
1. They were developed by the ICAR-National Soybean Research Institute, Indore.
2. Soybean is a rabi crop grown mainly in Punjab and Haryana.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 1 is correct. Soybean is a rain-fed kharif legume grown mainly in Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra and Rajasthan. The new varieties gave about 20 quintals per hectare even in a bad year (potential 22-25) against a national average of 10-11, which matters given India's edible-oil import dependence.

questions.q:
With reference to India's first National Household Travel Survey, consider the following statements:
1. It was conducted by NITI Aayog.
2. Cars are the most used mode for work trips.
3. A majority of workers use public transport to reach work.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: None is correct. The survey was conducted by the National Statistics Office. Two-wheelers account for 42.6% of work trips and cars only 3%, while just 9% of workers use public transport. Women depend more on buses (21.7% of urban women against 6.9% of men), and metro and suburban rail carry about 5% of urban commutes.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the RBI's new facility at Bhubaneswar:
1. It combines a data centre with a Cybersecurity Training Institute.
2. It is located away from the RBI's existing data centres in Maharashtra, partly to reduce seismic and border risk.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Both are correct. The Rs 169 crore facility will host critical systems such as NEFT, RTGS, the final settlement of UPI and e-Kuber, and train staff in AI, big data, quantum computing and blockchain. Geographic spread of data centres improves the resilience of payment systems.
